commit.message:
scripts: check release notes consistency in CI

The release note fragments in docs/release-notes/unreleased are only
consistent as long as the fragments are deleted once their change is
released, and a release is only cut after its fragments were folded into
its release note document. Nothing enforced either, so a forgotten step
would either announce a change twice or ship a release with incomplete
notes.

Add check-release-notes-consistency.sh with two modes. On pull requests, it
fails if a fragment belongs to a PR that is already announced in a
version-wide release note document, which catches both the fold and the
port of a patch release's notes to master. If the pull request bumps
build/version.go to a release version, release candidate or final, it also
requires the release note document of that version to exist and all
fragments to be folded into it. A final release additionally requires a
non-empty contributors section. The release mode runs the same readiness
check in the release build against the tagged commit.

The check runs in its own CI job that ignores the no-changelog label, since
the pull requests that fold fragments or bump the version carry that label.
Release branches keep their release version between releases, so the
readiness check only runs for the pull request that changes the version.

commit.message:
scripts: validate release note fragments in CI

The release note check only verified that the PR's link shows up somewhere
under docs/release-notes, so a fragment with the wrong filename, a missing
link or misspelled headings passed. Since the fragments are consolidated at
release time, such mistakes would only surface then.

Validate every file that a PR adds or modifies in a subdirectory of the
release notes against its base: it must live in unreleased/, start with a
top-level heading and only use the headings of the template or of the
newest version-wide release note document, without the document title or a
contributors section. A newly added fragment must additionally be named
after the PR and link to it. Modified fragments are exempt from that, so
that a follow-up PR can extend the entry of an earlier one.

The existing recursive link check is kept so that version-wide release note
files of older release lines continue to pass. The CI checkout now fetches
two commits so that the base of the PR's merge commit is available.

commit.message:
scripts: match exact PR number in release note check

The release note check used a plain substring match, so a PR whose number
is a prefix of another PR's number (e.g. 1132 and 11326) passed as soon as
the longer number was referenced. Require that the PR number isn't followed
by another digit.

commit.message:
docs: add per-PR release note fragments

Every PR currently edits the release note document of the next release and
its shared contributor list, so concurrent PRs keep conflicting on the same
lines. Following Bitcoin Core's release note process, new entries are
instead added as one fragment file per PR in docs/release-notes/unreleased.

The fragments are not tied to a release. Each one is folded into the release
note document of the first release that ships the change when that release
is prepared, and the contributor list is generated from Git history. This
means a contributor doesn't need to know whether the change will be
backported: the automated backport workflow cherry-picks the fragment along
with the change, so a backported fix ends up in the next patch release, and
the port of the patch release notes to master deletes the released
fragments there.

The existing release-notes-0.22.0.md and release-notes-0.21.5.md stay as the
baseline for the entries written before this change.

The guide lives in docs/release-notes/README.md. The pull request template,
contribution guidelines, backport workflow documentation and release note CI
failure message point contributors at it.

commit.message:
docs: add revocation validation release note

In this commit, we add the release note for the revocation validation and optional next revocation point updates.

htlcswitch: test unexpected revocation handling

In this commit, we add link-level coverage for the ReceiveRevocation
validation. The test verifies that the link reports ErrInvalidRevocation,
disconnects the peer, and leaves the channel open.

htlcswitch: run every TestChannelLinkFail case as a subtest

In this commit, we fix TestChannelLinkFail so it actually runs all of
its cases. The loop over the table would `return` as soon as it hit a
case that expects the link to stay up, which ended the whole test. As
the very first case (a warning message from the remote) is one of
those, none of the cases after it had been running, including the ones
that assert we force close on an invalid commit_sig.

We now run each case as a subtest, so the early return only ends that
case. All of the existing cases pass.

multi: make RemoteNextRevocation an fn.Option

In this commit, we change OpenChannel.RemoteNextRevocation and
ChannelCloseSummary.RemoteNextRevocation from a bare *btcec.PublicKey to
an fn.Option[btcec.PublicKey], and have
LightningChannel.RemoteNextRevocation return one as well. The remote
party's next revocation point is legitimately absent until they send
channel_ready (and, for taproot channels, until we have their nonces),
so the type should say so rather than leaving it to convention.

With an Option, code can no longer move the point into a field that
assumes it's always set without first deciding what to do when it's
absent. Every place that needs the point now has to unwrap it: the
revocation rotation, restoring a pending remote commitment, the anchor
resolution and chain watcher paths for a pending remote commitment, and
a retransmitted channel_ready in the peer. Each returns the new
ErrNoNextRevocation if it's missing. The presence checks in the funding
manager, link and peer become IsSome/IsNone.

We hold the key by value rather than by pointer, so a present point is
always a real key: there's no Some(nil) to fall into. In the same
spirit, InsertNextRevocation and InitNextRevocation now take the key by
value, which moves the only pointer dereference to the funding manager,
where the point comes straight off a decoded channel_ready message.

The on-disk format is unchanged. The revocation state still omits the
point when it's absent, and the close summary still writes a presence
flag ahead of it. The frozen migration packages keep their own copies of
these types, so they're untouched.

We add a round trip test for a channel with no next point, and for
close summaries with and without one. The peer test for a retransmitted
channel_ready previously passed a channel with no next point and
inserted an empty value. It now asserts that case is rejected, and that
a real point makes it into the peer's copy of the channel.

lnwallet: refine revocation validation order

In this commit, we refine revocation processing and extend its transition
coverage. The state-transition and key checks now run before their
corresponding revocation bookkeeping updates.

The tests cover the rejected cases for tweakless and taproot channels,
verify that their revocation bookkeeping stays unchanged, and confirm that
the next valid transition succeeds.

lncfg: derive MaxAllowedFeeRate from chainfee.FeePerKwCeiling

Both constants express the highest fee rate lnd will deliberately pay.
Derive MaxAllowedFeeRate from FeePerKwCeiling so the two values can
never diverge.

lnwallet/chainfee: clamp web API min relay feerate

The min_relay_feerate field of the --fee.url API response was returned
by RelayFeePerKW unclamped. Clamp it at the ingestion boundary to the
same bounds as the block target estimates: floored at FeePerKwFloor and
capped at FeePerKwCeiling.
docs: release notes for web API fee estimate ceiling

lnwallet/chainfee: clamp web API fee estimates to a ceiling

Fee rates returned by the external --fee.url API were only floor-clamped.
Clamp them to a new FeePerKwCeiling of 10,000 sat/vb, matching the highest
fee rate the sweeper can be configured with, so out-of-range values from
the external API are bounded before they propagate.
